## Home media

[[edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nineteen_Eighty-Four_(1984_film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section's source code: Home media")]

[International Video Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Video_Entertainment "International Video Entertainment") paid US$2 million for North American [home video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_video "Home video") rights, the fifth-biggest deal ever at the time.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen_Eighty-Four_(1984_film)#cite_note-hv-21) Their initial VHS & Betamax releases came out in 1985, with a later release in 1989. [Avid Home Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avid_Home_Entertainment "Avid Home Entertainment") released it on VHS in 1990 and again in 1994. In between the Avid releases, [GoodTimes Home Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoodTimes_Home_Video "GoodTimes Home Video") released a VHS in LP mode in 1992. After acquiring ITC Entertainment Group, [PolyGram Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PolyGram_Video "PolyGram Video") released their VHS in conjunction with [Sundance Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Channel_(United_States) "Sundance Channel (United States)") in 1996.

In 2003 [MGM Home Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MGM_Home_Entertainment "MGM Home Entertainment") released it on DVD in North America and in the UK a year later; the American DVD only contains Muldowney's score while the UK DVD contains the mix of his and Eurythmics' soundtrack. TGG Direct re-released it on DVD in 2013 as a double feature with Megaville. It has been released on Blu-ray twice, first by [Twilight Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight_Time_(home_video_label) "Twilight Time (home video label)") in 2015 as a limited 3,000-copy run and by [The Criterion Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Criterion_Collection "The Criterion Collection") in 2019. Both of these editions contain both the original theatrical Eurythmics score and the alternate Muldowney score.

In 2024 it was released on 4K [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") in Germany and Hungary.

**John Lawrence Russell** (January 3, 1921 – January 19, 1991) was an American film and television actor, most noted for his starring role as Marshal Dan Troop in the [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")[Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)") television series _[Lawman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawman\_(TV\_series) "Lawman (TV series)")_ from 1958 to 1962 and his lead role as international adventurer Tim Kelly in the syndicated TV series _[Soldiers of Fortune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldiers\_of\_Fortune\_(TV\_series) "Soldiers of Fortune (TV series)")_ from 1955 to 1957.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-ST-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Russell_(actor)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Born in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") to insurance company executive John Henry Russell and his wife, Amy Requa, John Lawrence Russell was the eldest of three children.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-3) He attended the [University of California, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles "University of California, Los Angeles") as a student athlete.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-4)

Following the start of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), he joined the [United States Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps"), though he was initially rejected because of his height (6 ft 3 in (1.91 m)).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-5) He was commissioned as a [second lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_lieutenant "Second lieutenant") on November 11, 1942, and was assigned to the [6th Marine Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6th_Marines "6th Marines"). His division was sent to [Guadalcanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalcanal "Guadalcanal"), where he served as an assistant [intelligence officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_officer "Intelligence officer"). He contracted [malaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaria "Malaria") and returned home with a medical discharge.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-6)

Publicity still with 1959 [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") series leads [Will Hutchins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Hutchins "Will Hutchins") (_[Sugarfoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarfoot "Sugarfoot")_), [Peter Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Brown_(actor) "Peter Brown (actor)") (_[Lawman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawman\_(TV\_series) "Lawman (TV series)")_), [Jack Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Kelly_(actor) "Jack Kelly (actor)") (_[Maverick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maverick\_(TV\_series) "Maverick (TV series)")_), [Ty Hardin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Hardin "Ty Hardin") (_[Bronco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronco\_(TV\_series) "Bronco (TV series)")_), [James Garner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Garner "James Garner") (_Maverick_), [Wayde Preston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayde_Preston "Wayde Preston")_([Colt .45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colt\_.45\_(TV\_series) "Colt .45 (TV series)")_), and John Russell (_[Lawman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawman\_(TV\_series) "Lawman (TV series)")_)

Russell signed a contract with [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox") in 1945 and made his first film appearance as a guard in _[A Royal Scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Royal\_Scandal\_(1945\_film) "A Royal Scandal (1945 film)")_. He played several supporting parts while at Fox, acting the role of a junior law partner in the Clifton Webb comedy _[Sitting Pretty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitting\_Pretty\_(1948\_film) "Sitting Pretty (1948 film)")_ (1948), as well as a navy pilot in _[Slattery's Hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slattery's\_Hurricane "Slattery's Hurricane")_ (1949). He primarily played secondary roles, often in [Western films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_film "Western film"), including [William A. Wellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_A._Wellman "William A. Wellman")'s 1948 _[Yellow Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow\_Sky "Yellow Sky")._ Later, however, he signed with [Republic Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Pictures "Republic Pictures"), where he was cast in a starring role opposite [Judy Canova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Canova "Judy Canova") in _[Oklahoma Annie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma\_Annie "Oklahoma Annie")_ (1952).

In 1955, Russell landed the lead role in a television drama series called _[Soldiers of Fortune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldiers\_of\_Fortune\_(TV\_series) "Soldiers of Fortune (TV series)")_. This half-hour syndicated adventure show placed his sidekick (played by [Chick Chandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Chandler "Chick Chandler")) and him in a dangerous setting each week. While the show proved popular with young boys, it did not draw enough adult viewers to its prime slot and was canceled in 1957. That same year, he returned to films briefly to appear as a corrupt agricultural magnate in the Warner Bros. low-budget exploitation film _[Untamed Youth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Untamed\_Youth "Untamed Youth")_. A year later, he returned to the small screen, as gunslinger Matt Reardon, in "The Empty Gun" episode of the [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")/Warner Bros. Western series, _[Cheyenne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne\_(1955\_TV\_series) "Cheyenne (1955 TV series)")_.

In 1958, he appeared as Saylor Hornbook on _Cheyenne_ in the episode titled "Dead to Rights". In 1958, he was cast in his best-known role: the stolid, taciturn Marshal Dan Troop, the lead character in _[Lawman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawman\_(TV\_series) "Lawman (TV series)")_, an ABC/[Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") hit Western series that ran for four years. Co-starring alongside [Peter Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Brown_(actor) "Peter Brown (actor)"), who played Deputy Johnny McKay, and [Peggie Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peggie_Castle "Peggie Castle") as Birdcage Saloon owner Lily Merrill, Russell portrayed a US frontier peace officer mentoring his younger compatriot. Russell also appeared in other motion pictures for Warner Bros., notably as a [Sioux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sioux "Sioux") chieftain in _[Yellowstone Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellowstone\_Kelly "Yellowstone Kelly")_ (1959) and as a rich, corrupt cattle rancher, Nathan Burdette, in the highly successful [Howard Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Hawks "Howard Hawks") Western _[Rio Bravo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio\_Bravo\_(film) "Rio Bravo (film)")_ (1959), starring [John Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne "John Wayne"). At the same time, Russell guest-starred in an episode of [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC")'s adventure series _[Northwest Passage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest\_Passage\_(TV\_series) "Northwest Passage (TV series)")_. In 1969, Russell appeared in five episodes of the [Robert Wagner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Wagner "Robert Wagner") series, _[It Takes a Thief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_Takes\_a\_Thief\_(1968\_TV\_series) "It Takes a Thief (1968 TV series)")_: "Guess Who's Coming To Rio?" (January 9, 1969), "Saturday Night in Venice" (September 25, 1969), "The Blue, Blue Danube" (October 30, 1969), "Payoff in The Piazza" (November 13, 1969), and "A Friend in Deed" (November 27, 1969).

Throughout the remainder of his movie career, he played secondary roles in more than 20 films, including several [A.C. Lyles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Lyles "A.C. Lyles") Westerns and three films directed by his friend, [Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood"), most notably as Marshal Stockburn, the chief villain in Eastwood's 1985 film _[Pale Rider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pale\_Rider "Pale Rider")_. Russell also appeared as Bloody Bill Anderson in Eastwood's 1976 Western _[The Outlaw Josey Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Outlaw\_Josey\_Wales "The Outlaw Josey Wales")_. He appeared in the second season of the [Filmation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmation "Filmation") children's science-fiction series _[Jason of Star Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason\_of\_Star\_Command "Jason of Star Command")_. He played Commander Stone, a blue-skinned alien from [Alpha Centauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_Centauri "Alpha Centauri").

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Russell_(actor)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Death")]

Russell died of complications from [emphysema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emphysema "Emphysema") in 1991, aged 70.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-ST-1)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-7)

**John Lawrence Russell** (January 3, 1921 – January 19, 1991) was an American film and television actor, most noted for his starring role as Marshal Dan Troop in the [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")[Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)") television series _[Lawman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawman\_(TV\_series) "Lawman (TV series)")_ from 1958 to 1962 and his lead role as international adventurer Tim Kelly in the syndicated TV series _[Soldiers of Fortune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldiers\_of\_Fortune\_(TV\_series) "Soldiers of Fortune (TV series)")_ from 1955 to 1957.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-ST-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Russell_(actor)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Born in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") to insurance company executive John Henry Russell and his wife, Amy Requa, John Lawrence Russell was the eldest of three children.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-3) He attended the [University of California, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles "University of California, Los Angeles") as a student athlete.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-4)

Following the start of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), he joined the [United States Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps"), though he was initially rejected because of his height (6 ft 3 in (1.91 m)).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-5) He was commissioned as a [second lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_lieutenant "Second lieutenant") on November 11, 1942, and was assigned to the [6th Marine Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6th_Marines "6th Marines"). His division was sent to [Guadalcanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalcanal "Guadalcanal"), where he served as an assistant [intelligence officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_officer "Intelligence officer"). He contracted [malaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaria "Malaria") and returned home with a medical discharge.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-6)

Publicity still with 1959 [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") series leads [Will Hutchins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Hutchins "Will Hutchins") (_[Sugarfoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarfoot "Sugarfoot")_), [Peter Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Brown_(actor) "Peter Brown (actor)") (_[Lawman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawman\_(TV\_series) "Lawman (TV series)")_), [Jack Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Kelly_(actor) "Jack Kelly (actor)") (_[Maverick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maverick\_(TV\_series) "Maverick (TV series)")_), [Ty Hardin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Hardin "Ty Hardin") (_[Bronco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronco\_(TV\_series) "Bronco (TV series)")_), [James Garner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Garner "James Garner") (_Maverick_), [Wayde Preston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayde_Preston "Wayde Preston")_([Colt .45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colt\_.45\_(TV\_series) "Colt .45 (TV series)")_), and John Russell (_[Lawman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawman\_(TV\_series) "Lawman (TV series)")_)

Russell signed a contract with [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox") in 1945 and made his first film appearance as a guard in _[A Royal Scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Royal\_Scandal\_(1945\_film) "A Royal Scandal (1945 film)")_. He played several supporting parts while at Fox, acting the role of a junior law partner in the Clifton Webb comedy _[Sitting Pretty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitting\_Pretty\_(1948\_film) "Sitting Pretty (1948 film)")_ (1948), as well as a navy pilot in _[Slattery's Hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slattery's\_Hurricane "Slattery's Hurricane")_ (1949). He primarily played secondary roles, often in [Western films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_film "Western film"), including [William A. Wellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_A._Wellman "William A. Wellman")'s 1948 _[Yellow Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow\_Sky "Yellow Sky")._ Later, however, he signed with [Republic Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Pictures "Republic Pictures"), where he was cast in a starring role opposite [Judy Canova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Canova "Judy Canova") in _[Oklahoma Annie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma\_Annie "Oklahoma Annie")_ (1952).

In 1955, Russell landed the lead role in a television drama series called _[Soldiers of Fortune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldiers\_of\_Fortune\_(TV\_series) "Soldiers of Fortune (TV series)")_. This half-hour syndicated adventure show placed his sidekick (played by [Chick Chandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_Chandler "Chick Chandler")) and him in a dangerous setting each week. While the show proved popular with young boys, it did not draw enough adult viewers to its prime slot and was canceled in 1957. That same year, he returned to films briefly to appear as a corrupt agricultural magnate in the Warner Bros. low-budget exploitation film _[Untamed Youth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Untamed\_Youth "Untamed Youth")_. A year later, he returned to the small screen, as gunslinger Matt Reardon, in "The Empty Gun" episode of the [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")/Warner Bros. Western series, _[Cheyenne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne\_(1955\_TV\_series) "Cheyenne (1955 TV series)")_.

In 1958, he appeared as Saylor Hornbook on _Cheyenne_ in the episode titled "Dead to Rights". In 1958, he was cast in his best-known role: the stolid, taciturn Marshal Dan Troop, the lead character in _[Lawman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawman\_(TV\_series) "Lawman (TV series)")_, an ABC/[Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") hit Western series that ran for four years. Co-starring alongside [Peter Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Brown_(actor) "Peter Brown (actor)"), who played Deputy Johnny McKay, and [Peggie Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peggie_Castle "Peggie Castle") as Birdcage Saloon owner Lily Merrill, Russell portrayed a US frontier peace officer mentoring his younger compatriot. Russell also appeared in other motion pictures for Warner Bros., notably as a [Sioux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sioux "Sioux") chieftain in _[Yellowstone Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellowstone\_Kelly "Yellowstone Kelly")_ (1959) and as a rich, corrupt cattle rancher, Nathan Burdette, in the highly successful [Howard Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Hawks "Howard Hawks") Western _[Rio Bravo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio\_Bravo\_(film) "Rio Bravo (film)")_ (1959), starring [John Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne "John Wayne"). At the same time, Russell guest-starred in an episode of [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC")'s adventure series _[Northwest Passage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest\_Passage\_(TV\_series) "Northwest Passage (TV series)")_. In 1969, Russell appeared in five episodes of the [Robert Wagner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Wagner "Robert Wagner") series, _[It Takes a Thief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_Takes\_a\_Thief\_(1968\_TV\_series) "It Takes a Thief (1968 TV series)")_: "Guess Who's Coming To Rio?" (January 9, 1969), "Saturday Night in Venice" (September 25, 1969), "The Blue, Blue Danube" (October 30, 1969), "Payoff in The Piazza" (November 13, 1969), and "A Friend in Deed" (November 27, 1969).

Throughout the remainder of his movie career, he played secondary roles in more than 20 films, including several [A.C. Lyles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Lyles "A.C. Lyles") Westerns and three films directed by his friend, [Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood"), most notably as Marshal Stockburn, the chief villain in Eastwood's 1985 film _[Pale Rider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pale\_Rider "Pale Rider")_. Russell also appeared as Bloody Bill Anderson in Eastwood's 1976 Western _[The Outlaw Josey Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Outlaw\_Josey\_Wales "The Outlaw Josey Wales")_. He appeared in the second season of the [Filmation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmation "Filmation") children's science-fiction series _[Jason of Star Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason\_of\_Star\_Command "Jason of Star Command")_. He played Commander Stone, a blue-skinned alien from [Alpha Centauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_Centauri "Alpha Centauri").

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Russell_(actor)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Death")]

Russell died of complications from [emphysema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emphysema "Emphysema") in 1991, aged 70.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-ST-1)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Russell_(actor)#cite_note-7)

_**Another Time, Another Place**_ is a 1983 British [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_film "Drama film") directed by Michael Radford and starring [Phyllis Logan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllis_Logan "Phyllis Logan"), Giovanni Mauriello and [Denise Coffey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denise_Coffey "Denise Coffey").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-BFIsearch-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-3) The screenplay was based on the 1983 novel by [Jessie Kesson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessie_Kesson "Jessie Kesson").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-5)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In Scotland in 1943 during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), Janie is a young Scottish housewife married to Dougal, who is 15 years older. Participating in a war rehabilitation program, the couple take in three Italian [prisoners of war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoners_of_war "Prisoners of war") to work on their farm. Janie soon falls in love with one of the three, Luigi. She begins a secret relationship with Luigi that is doomed from the start.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-7)

_**Another Time, Another Place**_ is a 1983 British [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_film "Drama film") directed by Michael Radford and starring [Phyllis Logan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllis_Logan "Phyllis Logan"), Giovanni Mauriello and [Denise Coffey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denise_Coffey "Denise Coffey").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-BFIsearch-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-3) The screenplay was based on the 1983 novel by [Jessie Kesson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessie_Kesson "Jessie Kesson").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-5)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In Scotland in 1943 during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), Janie is a young Scottish housewife married to Dougal, who is 15 years older. Participating in a war rehabilitation program, the couple take in three Italian [prisoners of war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoners_of_war "Prisoners of war") to work on their farm. Janie soon falls in love with one of the three, Luigi. She begins a secret relationship with Luigi that is doomed from the start.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-7)

**John Francis Lane** (1 December 1928 – 15 January 2018)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-2) was an English journalist, critic and actor. He was known for being a small-part actor in many [Italian films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_Italy "Cinema of Italy"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-3) and as a contributor to _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ writing obituaries for Italian cultural figures.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Mayes-1)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Francis_Lane&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Lane was born in [Tankerton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tankerton "Tankerton"), a suburb of [Whitstable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitstable "Whitstable") in [Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent "Kent"), to a middle-class family in 1928. He became a boarder at the [Royal Grammar School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Grammar_School_Worcester "Royal Grammar School Worcester") in [Worcester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester,_England "Worcester, England"), and towards the end of the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") attended [Dulwich College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulwich_College "Dulwich College") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4) He then had a spell as a stage manager in London's [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_of_London "West End of London").

Lane first visited Italy in 1949, following a German boyfriend from Paris, where he was then studying at the [Sorbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Paris "University of Paris"). After learning Italian at the [University of Florence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Florence "University of Florence"), he had settled in Rome by 1951, finding Italy more tolerant of his homosexuality than the Britain of the time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Mayes-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4) Learning Italian in Florence, he became entranced by the country after seeing [Franco Zeffirelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Zeffirelli "Franco Zeffirelli")'s production of _[Troilus and Cressida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troilus\_and\_Cressida "Troilus and Cressida")_. Zeffirelli later became one of his boyfriends.

He was made a [Cavaliere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavaliere "Cavaliere") in the 1975 Italian Order of Merit.

In retirement Lane lived in the town of [Rende](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rende "Rende") in the region of [Calabria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabria "Calabria"). He wrote frequently on Italian life for _[The Economist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Economist "The Economist")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Mayes-1) His memoir, _To Each His Own Dolce Vita_, was published in 2013.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4)

Lane died in January 2018 in [Cosenza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosenza "Cosenza") in southern Italy.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-5) Knowledge he had died was delayed and only emerged following the end of Zeffirelli's life.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4)

**John Francis Lane** (1 December 1928 – 15 January 2018)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-2) was an English journalist, critic and actor. He was known for being a small-part actor in many [Italian films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_Italy "Cinema of Italy"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-3) and as a contributor to _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ writing obituaries for Italian cultural figures.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Mayes-1)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Francis_Lane&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Lane was born in [Tankerton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tankerton "Tankerton"), a suburb of [Whitstable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitstable "Whitstable") in [Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent "Kent"), to a middle-class family in 1928. He became a boarder at the [Royal Grammar School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Grammar_School_Worcester "Royal Grammar School Worcester") in [Worcester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester,_England "Worcester, England"), and towards the end of the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") attended [Dulwich College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulwich_College "Dulwich College") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4) He then had a spell as a stage manager in London's [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_of_London "West End of London").

Lane first visited Italy in 1949, following a German boyfriend from Paris, where he was then studying at the [Sorbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Paris "University of Paris"). After learning Italian at the [University of Florence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Florence "University of Florence"), he had settled in Rome by 1951, finding Italy more tolerant of his homosexuality than the Britain of the time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Mayes-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4) Learning Italian in Florence, he became entranced by the country after seeing [Franco Zeffirelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Zeffirelli "Franco Zeffirelli")'s production of _[Troilus and Cressida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troilus\_and\_Cressida "Troilus and Cressida")_. Zeffirelli later became one of his boyfriends.

He was made a [Cavaliere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavaliere "Cavaliere") in the 1975 Italian Order of Merit.

In retirement Lane lived in the town of [Rende](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rende "Rende") in the region of [Calabria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabria "Calabria"). He wrote frequently on Italian life for _[The Economist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Economist "The Economist")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Mayes-1) His memoir, _To Each His Own Dolce Vita_, was published in 2013.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4)

Lane died in January 2018 in [Cosenza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosenza "Cosenza") in southern Italy.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-5) Knowledge he had died was delayed and only emerged following the end of Zeffirelli's life.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4)

**John Francis Lane** (1 December 1928 – 15 January 2018)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-2) was an English journalist, critic and actor. He was known for being a small-part actor in many [Italian films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_Italy "Cinema of Italy"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-3) and as a contributor to _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ writing obituaries for Italian cultural figures.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Mayes-1)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Francis_Lane&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Lane was born in [Tankerton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tankerton "Tankerton"), a suburb of [Whitstable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitstable "Whitstable") in [Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent "Kent"), to a middle-class family in 1928. He became a boarder at the [Royal Grammar School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Grammar_School_Worcester "Royal Grammar School Worcester") in [Worcester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester,_England "Worcester, England"), and towards the end of the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") attended [Dulwich College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulwich_College "Dulwich College") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4) He then had a spell as a stage manager in London's [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_of_London "West End of London").

Lane first visited Italy in 1949, following a German boyfriend from Paris, where he was then studying at the [Sorbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Paris "University of Paris"). After learning Italian at the [University of Florence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Florence "University of Florence"), he had settled in Rome by 1951, finding Italy more tolerant of his homosexuality than the Britain of the time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Mayes-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4) Learning Italian in Florence, he became entranced by the country after seeing [Franco Zeffirelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Zeffirelli "Franco Zeffirelli")'s production of _[Troilus and Cressida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troilus\_and\_Cressida "Troilus and Cressida")_. Zeffirelli later became one of his boyfriends.

He was made a [Cavaliere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavaliere "Cavaliere") in the 1975 Italian Order of Merit.

In retirement Lane lived in the town of [Rende](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rende "Rende") in the region of [Calabria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabria "Calabria"). He wrote frequently on Italian life for _[The Economist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Economist "The Economist")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Mayes-1) His memoir, _To Each His Own Dolce Vita_, was published in 2013.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4)

Lane died in January 2018 in [Cosenza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosenza "Cosenza") in southern Italy.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-5) Knowledge he had died was delayed and only emerged following the end of Zeffirelli's life.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Lane#cite_note-Timesobit-4)
